- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes — model tends to overcorrect downward; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast if sentiment dips below 0.3.
- Lagged mean reversion bias: if 3–5 days of downward trend, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment > 0.6 and price rises > 2%, cap forecast at +1.5–2.0% above peak to avoid overcorrection.
- Ignore sentiment-driven volatility in early forecast horizon (1–3 days) — sentiment has low predictive power; use only 5+ day sentiment for correction.
- If sentiment is consistently low (< 0.2) and price is trending up, model underestimates — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to avoid missing rally.
- Forecast should not drop below 10% below 10-day moving average unless sentiment confirms bearish shift.
